doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Still touring at 81 and the travel as the real job
summary: He is slowing down; travel is the hard, paid part while the gig is the fun part.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And you’re still touring? Good for you, man. I think it keeps you young I believe.
Well mentally yeah, but your body just gets to be old, you know, before you know it. I feel old today you know because I’ve got a cough. And I’m 81 now you know so things © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

go wrong you know but it’s still a good feeling when you get out there and play your horn, you know, you feel it. But the traveling part gets to be a very difficult job you know, so I’m having to slow down but I still love the music, still love to play.

I was thinking about that, if you did the math about how many hours you spend getting to a gig, getting home from a gig, getting from one to another, and then you balance it with what — the time you’re actually on stage having a great time.

Yeah. We often talk about that, all the time, you know say the real job, what we really get paid for is the travel. But it’s what you do for free is the gig. But you know that’s always fun. When it’s over with, back to the traveling. You’ve got to go back to the hotel and pack your stuff and get ready to go. And that’s the job again. So it’s two aspects of it, and one aspect is harder than the other, but you love the other so much that you’d do it for free, you know.
